page.layout: One printed page. Running head at top with page number 50 at left. Main text in one column of paragraphs, with italic verse lines below. Left margin holds one marginal note "Pluuias & rores suppeditat." beside the second paragraph. Catchword "Perfusa" at lower right, set after the verse.

main_text.p: tumuis fæuas & efferas à Dei nutu pendere, & sub eius imperio esse ac potestate, vt iis ad quodcunque voluerit opus, siue seruandis iis qui in ipso spem suam collocant, siue perden- dis impiis aduersus nomen eius blasphemis vtatur: Et quanuis in magnas iras efferbue- rint, solo tamè ipsius verbo frangi & ita coer- ceri vt nulla furoris appareant vestigia.

Pluuias & rores suppeditat.Nec vero silentio prætereundum est ex aëre nobis thesauros illos ingentes rorum & plu- uiarum prouenire, quibus terra per se arida, rigatur & diluitur & ita fœcundatur vt semina quæ sinu eius continentur & fouentur, puta hordeum, frumentum & cætera, germinent, crescat & fructum ferant, quod & ipsum Da- uid Psalm.65. sic enarrat.

l.i: Tu rura ex solio despicis aureo,
Nec curare prius tot fata desinis
Anni sic abeunt, sic redeunt tuis
Dum tu summe Pater celsus inambulas,

page.notes: The margin note "Pluuias & rores suppeditat." is set in small type at left, beside the second paragraph. The verse lines are italic and may carry printing errors (for example "beet", "Demessa", "inambulas") that are reproduced as printed. The word "Perfusa" at lower right is the catchword, although it reads as the start of the next line; it is kept here as printed.
